sentences.text: Martin Van Buren -LRB- Maarten van Buren ; December 5 , 1782 -- July 24 , 1862 -RRB- was an American politician who served as the eighth President of the United States -LRB- 1837 -- 41 -RRB- .	politician	politician	eighth President of the United States	List of Presidents of the United States

A member of the Democratic Party , he served in a number of other senior roles , including eighth Vice President -LRB- 1833 -- 37 -RRB- and tenth Secretary of State -LRB- 1829 -- 31 -RRB- , both under Andrew Jackson .	Andrew Jackson	Andrew Jackson	Democratic	Democratic Party (United States)	Democratic Party	Democratic Party (United States)	Vice President	Vice President of the United States	Secretary of State	United States Secretary of State
Van Buren won the presidency by promising to continue Jackson 's policies .

Shortly after taking office , the Panic of 1837 struck the nation , and his inability to deal effectively with the economic crisis , combined with the growing political strength of the opposition Whig Party , led to his defeat in the 1840 presidential election .	Panic of 1837	Panic of 1837	Whig Party	Whig Party (United States)	1840 presidential election	United States presidential election, 1840

During his half-century of public service , he built , perfected , and defended a new system of political parties at first the state and then the federal level .	state	U.S. state	federal	United States federal government

In New York he reorganized the Democratic-Republican Party and established the Albany Regency to keep it in power .	Democratic-Republican	Democratic-Republican Party	Democratic	Democratic Party (United States)	New York	New York (state)	Democratic-Republican Party	Democratic-Republican Party	Albany Regency	Albany Regency

He then moved on Washington where he did more than anyone to construct the modern Democratic Party which dominated American politics down to the American Civil War .	Democratic	Democratic Party (United States)	Democratic Party	Democratic Party (United States)	 Washington	Washington, D.C.	modern Democratic Party	History of the Democratic Party (United States)	American Civil War	American Civil War
A delegate to a political convention at age 18 , he quickly moved from local to state politics , gaining fame both as a political organizer and an accomplished lawyer .	state	U.S. state

Elected to the Senate by the New York State Legislature in 1821 , Van Buren supported William H. Crawford for president in the 1824 election , but by 1828 had come to support Jackson .	New York	New York (state)	New York State Legislature	New York State Legislature	William H. Crawford	William H. Crawford	1824 election	United States presidential election, 1824	1828	United States presidential election, 1828

Van Buren was a major supporter and organizer for Jackson in the 1828 election , and ran for Governor of New York in the hope of using his personal popularity to boost Jackson 's campaign .	New York	New York (state)	1828	United States presidential election, 1828	Governor of New York	Governor of New York
Jackson and Van Buren were elected , and after serving as governor for two months , Van Buren resigned to become Jackson 's Secretary of State .	Secretary of State	United States Secretary of State

During Jackson 's eight years as president , Van Buren was a key advisor , and built the organizational structure for the coalescing Democratic Party , particularly in New York .	Democratic	Democratic Party (United States)	New York	New York (state)	Democratic Party	Democratic Party (United States)

In 1831 , following his resignation as Secretary of State , which aided Jackson in resolving the Petticoat affair , Jackson gave Van Buren a recess appointment as American minister to Britain .	Secretary of State	United States Secretary of State	Petticoat affair	Petticoat affair	recess appointment	recess appointment	American minister to Britain	United States Ambassador to the United Kingdom

Van Buren 's nomination was rejected by the Senate , cutting short his service in London , but he was elected vice president in the 1832 election .	1832 election	United States presidential election, 1832

Van Buren faced little opposition for the presidential nomination at the 1835 Democratic National Convention , and he defeated several Whig opponents in the 1836 presidential election .	Democratic	Democratic Party (United States)	1835 Democratic National Convention	1835 Democratic National Convention	1836 presidential election	United States presidential election, 1836
He was the first president to be born a United States citizen .	United States citizen	Natural-born-citizen clause

Of Dutch ancestry , he is the only president who spoke English as a second language , and was the first not to have a university degree or a military commission .	Dutch ancestry	Dutch people	English as a second language	English as a second language
As president , Van Buren was blamed for the depression of 1837 ; hostile newspapers called him `` Martin Van Ruin '' .

He attempted to cure the economic problems by keeping control of federal funds in an independent treasury , rather than in state banks , but Congress would not approve of this until 1840 .	state	U.S. state	federal	United States federal government	independent treasury	Independent Treasury

In foreign affairs , he denied the application of Texas for admission to the Union , unwilling to upset the balance of free and slave states in the Missouri Compromise , and hoping to avoid war with Mexico over Texas annexation .	Texas	Texas	Missouri Compromise	Missouri Compromise	Union	Union (American Civil War)
Additionally , relations with Britain and its colonies in Canada proved to be strained from the bloodless Aroostook War and the Caroline Affair .	Canada	Canada	Aroostook War	Aroostook War

In the 1840 election , Van Buren was voted out of office , losing to Whig candidate William Henry Harrison .	William Henry Harrison	William Henry Harrison	1840 election	United States presidential election, 1840

Van Buren was the leading candidate for the Democratic nomination in 1844 , but lost to James K. Polk , who went on to win the election .	Democratic	Democratic Party (United States)	Democratic nomination in 1844	1844 Democratic National Convention	James K. Polk	James K. Polk	went on to win the election	United States presidential election, 1844

In the 1848 election Van Buren ran unsuccessfully as the candidate of the anti-slavery Free Soil Party .	Free Soil	Free Soil Party	1848 election	United States presidential election, 1848	Free Soil Party	Free Soil Party

He returned to the Democratic fold to endorse Franklin Pierce -LRB- 1852 -RRB- , James Buchanan -LRB- 1856 -RRB- , and Stephen A. Douglas -LRB- 1860 -RRB- for the presidency .	Democratic	Democratic Party (United States)	Franklin Pierce	Franklin Pierce	James Buchanan	James Buchanan	Stephen A. Douglas	Stephen A. Douglas

However , his increasingly abolitionist views and support for the Union led him to support Abraham Lincoln 's policies after the start of the American Civil War .	Abraham	Abraham Van Buren	American Civil War	American Civil War	abolitionist	abolitionism	Union	Union (American Civil War)	Abraham Lincoln	Abraham Lincoln
Van Buren 's health began to fail in 1861 , and he died in July 1862 at age 79 .
